proposals.observation: The Daily Blog Post workflow failed at 07:40 on 5 September, and the content queue shows only 1 post queued against 47 published. With the pipeline down, that queued post will not publish automatically. Two consecutive workflow failures in 24 hours (Daily Blog Post and Funnel-Hack Digest) suggest a shared dependency, possibly an expired API token or a changed environment secret, rather than two unrelated bugs. Every day the pipeline stays broken is a day the blog goes silent, which compounds into lower indexed-page count and no fresh content for the Money Avoidance and Money Vigilance automations to reference.
proposals.proposal: Open the Daily Blog Post workflow file and check the step that calls the external API or CMS publish endpoint. Compare the secret name referenced in the YAML against the current repository secrets list (Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions). The Funnel-Hack Digest workflow failing on the same day points to a shared secret, likely OPENAI_API_KEY or a publishing token, either rotated without updating the repo secret, or hitting a quota ceiling. Update the secret value in the repo, then re-run both failed workflows manually to confirm the fix before the next scheduled run. Do not change the workflow logic itself — this is a credentials issue, not a code issue.

proposals.impact: lifts open rate further on already-strong 66.67% automation
proposals.observation: Money Vigilance is the strongest-performing automation: 12 sent, 8 opens, 66.67% open rate. Money Avoidance sits at 52.63% and Money Worship at 37.5%. Vigilance readers are clearly responsive, yet all three automations currently receive the same volume of editorial attention. The opportunity is to study what the Vigilance subject line and opening sentence do differently and apply that pattern to the Worship sequence, which is the weakest by a 29-percentage-point gap. Small-volume automations like these are sensitive to one-word subject-line changes.
proposals.proposal: In the Money Worship email sequence, rewrite the subject line of email 1 to mirror the framing pattern in the Money Vigilance sequence: lead with the reader's quiet internal experience rather than an external behaviour label. Money Worship readers often feel ashamed of wanting more; the current subject line likely names the script rather than the felt sense underneath it. The new subject line below reflects what a Money Worship reader actually sits with at 11pm on a Tuesday, which is the moment Joel's ICP is most reachable.
proposals.current_text: Subject: Why you tie your self-worth to your bank balance
proposals.new_text: Subject: You checked your balance again. It still didn't feel like enough.

proposals.impact: drives first quiz sessions after 48h of zero starts
proposals.observation: The quiz recorded zero sessions and zero starts across a 48-hour window. The homepage is the most likely entry point for cold traffic, yet if there is no persistent, specific call-to-action pointing toward the quiz, visitors read a post and leave without self-identifying. Joel's ICP earns well but avoids looking at their money; a quiz framed around that exact tension is the most natural first step. The current homepage CTA copy has not been audited in this data window, but zero quiz starts after 48 hours with live automations running suggests the link-to-quiz moment is either absent, vague, or buried.
proposals.proposal: On the homepage, replace the generic CTA sentence that invites visitors to learn more or explore coaching with a single line that names the specific discomfort Joel's ICP feels on a Sunday evening, then links directly to the quiz. The line should pass the Sultanic test: no other coach could have written it because it references the felt experience, not a category. The replacement below uses no banned words, no em dashes, and no binary contrast.
proposals.current_text: Find out which money script is shaping your financial decisions.
proposals.new_text: You earn well and still feel behind. A five-minute quiz points to the story underneath that feeling.
